items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: we were paying back the money that Mrs. Americus had advanced us to come to New York

ctx.x: Mr. Buchanan had given us the name of Lloyd Scott and his Bright Boys, because we were always doing something new in the line of entertaining while playing without making a number real showy. In "Lawd Lawd", we all had little washboards on which we scratched the rhythm behind the scat singing of Frank Newton and the baritone sax of Cecil. Sometimes, there would be a sharp whistle at the end of some chorus before a soloist would come in for the next chorus. Once we cooked up a gimmick on "Tiger Rag": When it came…

During these months at the "Track" which was the nickname for the Savoy, (because it was as exciting for some people to come there as it was to go to the race track), we were paying back the money that Mrs. Americus had advanced us to come to New York and other debts we owed in Springfield. Our salary was 40 dollars a week which I thought was good at the time, and it was coming in regularly. I had never worked such a long time at such a salary and if I had not been a great spender, I could have had a quite nice…

I had written to Wurlitzer in Cincinnati where I had bought the new trumpet on credit when my other one had gotten smashed, to let them know where I was. I thought that they would send someone from their company in New York to give me information on how I could continue paying for my horn but I never heard from the, and no-one ever came to see me about the payment which really did not worry me in the least.
